label: copy-phase input d with j coming up in the output
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only (98% of steps, 99% of mass) when the fed-back input is d, i.e. right after the model has output d. It is silent in the original and delimiter phases and essentially silent at recall_idx 0-1. But only about 1 in 8 copy-phase d inputs activate (precision 0.13 for the plain d-in-copy predicate). Magnitude is driven by an upcoming j: the top activations (0.8-1.0 of max) are all d followed by j in the original (d j j, d j t, ...). out_tok == j alone holds 47% of the mass at precision 0.71. Activations are also more common when d was original token 2 or 3 (recall_idx 3-4). Weak activations (<0.1 of max) occur on d inputs with no j nearby, where the gating is not captured. Rare weak firings happen on j inputs that follow d. The predicate (d input, j within the next 3 outputs) captures about 2/3 of the mass; the broader d-in-copy predicate captures 99% of the mass but has low precision.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=d (+8.87), phase=2 & in_tok=j (+4.71), in_tok=d (+4.04), next_out=j (+3.25), phase=2 & out_tok=j (+2.90), out_tok=j (+2.74). Lower it: out_tok=x (-3.78), prev_tok=<DEL> (-3.68), recall_idx=1 (-3.68), next_out=x (-3.48).
